notes: The authored legendary encounters: the lake trio (docs/mechanics/WATER_MAP.md section 5), the four bespoke concepts (docs/world-building/STRUCTURE_DECISIONS.md section 4, docs/story/ENCOUNTERS.md:392-395) and the wake of the sleeping Celebi (data/sapling_celebi.json, EXP-023). Every other legendary is Tier B: paste a structure into a fitting biome and gate it by badge count, and none of that is here.

A legendary is an ENTITY, so a re-export erases it and it is summoned over RCON by tools/reapply.py (step R14L), never by a pack: `spawnpokemonat` inside a function spawns nothing until a /reload (EXP-046 question 1). The pack does what functions can: the chamber's blocks, the gate, the keeper.
Ground is the canonical heightmap through tools/ground.py, rounded, never a world (CLAUDE.md's ground rule). Every mouth_y and portal_y in this file is measured, not authored.

The chambers are parametric, not a noise model: a stone envelope filled first, then the void carved out of it. That is what makes the seal provable offline (tools/legendaries_audit.py) instead of needing a dilation over a world.

Each record's `status` decides whether tools/legendaries.py emits it. `sited` is emitted; anything else is data only and the generator refuses to write its blocks (fail closed), so a blocked site cannot reach a world by accident.
period_why: the driver is one `execute positioned ... if entity @a[distance=..R]` line per emitted encounter, rescheduled every 20 ticks, so six encounters cost six command lines a second, not sixty a tick. The Celebi keeper's shape (tools/sapling_celebi.py), chosen because docs/mechanics/TOWN_TICK_BUDGET.md is counting the idle floor.

defaults.shell_margin_why: docs/mechanics/WATER_BUILD_PLAN.md 4.5 audit 1: at least 4 blocks of rock round every void, no void connecting to the water but the passage. Here it is guaranteed by construction: the envelope is filled solid first and extends shell_margin beyond every carved block in all six directions.
defaults.pool_depth_why: the flooded passage must meet the pool below the pool's surface: pool_depth must exceed bore - 1, so 4 with a bore of 3.
defaults.clearance_why: the envelope's top must stand shell_margin + clearance_blocks below the LOWEST heightmap ground over its own footprint, so no chamber roof thins under a slope and no chamber breaks a lake bed.
defaults.sleeve_flatness_why: the shaft's sleeve is filled to the lowest ground over its footprint, so it never raises the bed; the mouth may stand at most this far above that, which bounds the unsleeved lip of the hole.
defaults.light_why: docs/STATE.md, 'Places are lit as towns': lanterns, never light blocks.

A legendary authored above the cap of its own badge gate is therefore uncatchable, which would make the encounter a wall rather than a reward.

encounters.title: The wake of the Celebi in the Route 1 sapling
encounters.level_basis: the level data/sapling_celebi.json already summons it at; unchanged here. Above every provisional cap, so it is uncatchable as it stands: trainer-balance-designer must decide whether the wake lowers it or whether Celebi is a battle and not a catch.
encounters.blocked_why: The trigger is not settled. EXP-023's untested candidate was `minecraft:item_used_on_block` on the branch, with an item predicate and the progression flag. Two things were established here and neither closes it: (a) `minecraft:item_used_on_block` is a real vanilla advancement trigger and a location-triggered advancement is already proven in this repo as a per-player, once-only carrier (tools/rewards_pack.py, ADR-002), so the MECHANISM can carry a wake; (b) an advancement fires once per player for ever and its criteria cannot test another advancement, so an advancement whose criterion is only 'used item X on block Y' is BURNED by a player who tries the right item before the gate is open, and that player can never wake it. That is a real fault, not a detail, and it cannot be settled offline: it needs either a second criterion the repo has not used, or a tick-driven check like this pack's own gate. WHICH ITEM is also undecided, and no document names one.

gate.why: the Celebi belongs to the mainline arc (docs/story/FUTURE_SIDE_CONTENT.md) and its story line is Codex's (ARC.md). A late gate is this file's proposal only.

encounters.opens: the barrier shell tools/sapling_celebi.py writes round the branch (its shell_box), and the dormant flags on the Celebi itself
encounters.why: The sleeping Celebi is inert and walled in barriers precisely because Cobblemon ignores Invulnerable and a sword killed it (EXP-023). The wake is the moment those barriers come off, so it cannot be built before the trigger is chosen: the wall is the only thing protecting it.

open_questions: Shared or per player? An entity's NBT is world state, so a qualified player who opens a grotto's inner door opens it for everyone standing in the chamber, and the first catch takes the encounter for the whole server. docs/mechanics/WATER_MAP.md decision 1 leaves this open for the trio and ENCOUNTERS.md:397 leaves it open for Lugia. Nothing here decides it; the build is shared, and per player would need the scene runtime's per-player actors (EXP-034, which needs a second account).

A woken legendary can be killed. Cobblemon's PokemonEntity ignores Invulnerable and a sword killed the Celebi in three hits (EXP-023). While a chamber is shut the barrier door or the stone plug is the protection; once open, the legendary is as killable as any placed Pokemon. The re-application restores it, but within a session it is gone and the keeper cannot summon it back (functions cannot run Cobblemon's spawn command, EXP-046). No answer is proposed here.
The level cap. Every level in this file rests on an unread number (see level_caps.source). If a legendary is authored above its gate's cap it cannot be caught at all.
The badge gates of the four bespoke encounters are this file's proposals. Only the trio's (3, 5, 7) and Lugia's (Dive and champion_cleared) are the owner's.
